meta.title: Time of Day & Seasons
meta.description: The run has a live clock and a four-season year. Time is mostly atmospheric — it tints the world from dawn gold through day, sunset and night — but the season you're in shows on your status screen, changes the hub's music, and (in EX) determines which seasonal Pokémon can be found in the wild. The clock, seasons and all their behaviour are identical between the versions; only the seasonal species that EX adds are new.

prose.heading: Time sets the mood, not the rules
prose.text: The in-game clock drives the look of the world: the overworld and battle palettes smoothly blend through six keyframe tints — night, sunrise, daylight, sunset and back to night — as the minutes pass. It does not, however, change the route tables themselves — the same species are listed at any hour (in EX the clock does gate the time-of-day form of a few species, such as Lycanroc and Rockruff). What the clock and the season do change: the season stamp on your run's status screen, the hub's music, and — in EX — which seasonal or time-of-day forms of certain species can be found.

prose.heading: A day goes by quickly
prose.text: A run begins at 10:00. Every time you move between rooms during the run, one hour passes, so a full classic run is roughly one in-game day. In the hub, time moves more slowly — a quarter hour per room change. When the clock rolls past midnight, a day is counted; every two days the season advances, so a long campaign of runs takes you from spring through winter and around again.

prose.heading: Choose when you wake up
prose.text: The bed in your home is the run's time machine. Lying down asks what time you'd like to wake up — Dawn, Day, Dusk or Night — and which season, letting you set the hub's clock and season before a run. In multiplayer, the host's time and season are the ones everyone shares.

records.name: Palette tints
records.description: The overworld and battle palettes are tinted by a six-keyframe lookup: 5:00 night, 6:00 sunrise, 8:00 daylight, 19:00 daylight, 21:00 sunset, 23:00 night. Between keyframes the colour is interpolated frame by frame, so sunsets and dawns fade smoothly. Indoor maps are never tinted, and the tint can be temporarily disabled while a special visual is active.
records.source: src/rogue_timeofday.c @vanilla L93-134 (sToDPaletteLookup keyframes), L500-561 (interpolation between keyframes) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_timeofday.c @vanilla L427-438 (indoor maps excluded, temp-disable switch) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Time codes (Dawn/Day/Dusk/Night)
records.description: The clock maps to four named periods: Dawn 6:00–8:00, Day 8:00–21:00, Dusk 21:00–23:00 and Night 23:00–6:00. The period is taken from the start of the active keyframe interval, so the 19:00–21:00 fade is still counted as Day while the colour drifts toward sunset. These labels appear in the bed's wake-up menu; the run's status screen shows the season name and a numeric clock instead.

records.name: The run clock
records.description: A run always starts at 10:00. Each room change during an active run adds one hour, so a run covers roughly one in-game day from morning through the night. When the clock wraps past 24:00 a new day is counted and the season day-counter advances.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L3328 (run start: RogueToD_SetTime(60 × 10)), L5686-5688 (+60 min per warp while a run is active) / @origin/expansion L3315, L5677-5679; src/rogue_timeofday.c @vanilla L152-165 (time set with 24h wrap and day counter increment) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: The hub clock
records.description: In the hub (outside a run) time moves a quarter hour per room change, so the hub's time of day drifts slowly as you explore between runs. In a multiplayer hub, clients simply adopt the host's time and season.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L5713-5720 / @origin/expansion L5704-5711 (hub: clients copy host time/season, host +15 min per warp)

records.name: Waking up (time presets)
records.description: The bed in your home asks 'What time would you like to wake up?' with four presets: Dawn (6:00), Day (8:00), Dusk (21:00) and Night (23:00). It then asks which season you'd like to wake up in, and the hub adopts both — your chosen clock time and season carry the hub forward until the next room changes drift it.
records.source: data/maps/Rogue_Area_Home/scripts.pory @vanilla L400-430 (bed: time + season multichoice) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_script.c @vanilla L1227-1241 (Rogue_SetTimeAndSeason) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_timeofday.c @vanilla L214-235 (presets map to the 6:00/8:00/21:00/23:00 keyframes) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Seasons
records.description: The year cycles Spring → Summer → Autumn → Winter, and each season lasts two in-game days (so the season changes every two days on the run clock). Your current season is stamped on the run's status screen alongside the clock and badges, and the hub's music changes with it: spring plays a New Bark Town–style theme, summer Sandgem Town, autumn Floaroma Town and winter Snowpoint Town.
records.source: src/rogue_timeofday.c @vanilla L62 (DAYS_PER_SEASON 2), L180-212 (season from day counter) (identical @origin/expansion); include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L847-851 / @origin/expansion L849-853 (season enum); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L2929-2945 (season stamp on the status screen), L915-930 (seasonal hub music) / @origin/expansion L2916-2932, L915-930

records.name: Always-winter maps
records.description: Two snowy maps ignore the season clock for display purposes and always render as winter: Route 217 and Mt. Coronet. Their snow stays put even in summer.
records.source: src/rogue_timeofday.c @vanilla L197-206 (GetVisualSeason forces winter for the two snowy layouts) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Seasonal forms in the wild (EX)
records.description: In EX, certain species are gated by season and time of day when wild encounters are rolled. Deerling and Sawsbuck appear only in their own seasonal form (spring form in spring, and so on for the summer, autumn and winter forms). All three Lycanroc forms are in the wild pool, each locked to its own time slot: the daytime form only at Dawn or Day, the Dusk form only at Dusk, the Midnight form only at Night. Rockruff is time-gated too: the regular form never appears at Dusk, and the Own Tempo form only appears at Dusk.
